BY ADV UNNIKRISHNAN.V.ALAPATT

THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 06.02.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA.400/2016  2  2025:KER:16357 Joseph vs Sivaraj on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8252865/
1  JUDGMENT Dated this the 6th day of February, 2025
The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.604/2011 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Irinjalakuda is the appellant herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 14.3.2011.

According to the petitioner, on 14.3.2011 at about 1.45 p.m., while he was riding a bicycle through Vazhiyambalalm-Alathur road, a motor cycle bearing registration No.KL7 AD-638 ridden by the 2 nd respondent came from the opposite direction and hit him down and as a result of the accident,
the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
3.
The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2 nd respondent is the driver, 3rd respondent is the insurer and 4th respondent is the insured of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the 2025:KER:16357 negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.3,00,000/-.
4.
The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimony of PW1 and and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A9.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,75,150/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

9. Heard Sri. P.V. Baby, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri.
Unnikrishnan V. Alapatt, the learned Standing 2025:KER:16357 Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
10. The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.

According to him, the petitioner was working as driver of LMV Joseph vs Sivaraj on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8252865/
2 goods carrier, earning Rs.16,000/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.5,000/-.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the Tribunal is reasonable.
11. It is true that the petitioner could not prove his income, as claimed in the OP.
Petitioner was the owner cum driver of LMV goods carrier.
It is proved by Exhibit A8 RC Book and Exhibit A9 copy of driving licence.
Hence, from Exhibit A8 and A9, it is proved that the petitioner was a Driver of LMV goods carrier by profession.

As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13)
SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2011 will come to Rs.8,000/- Therefore, the petitioner being a Driver of LMV goods carrier by profession, his notional income is fixed at Rs.10,000/-, for the purpose of computing the 2025:KER:16357 loss of disability.

sentences.text:
12. In the accident, the petitioner sustained the following injuries:t "1. Malunited fracture of (L)
femur with implant in situ 2. Shortening of 1" of (L) femoral component compared to right 3. Limitation of abduction of (L) hip 4. Weakness of abduction of (L) hip 5. Limitation of flexion of (L) knee 6. Weakness of (R) quadriceps."
13. As per Exhibit A5 disability certificate issued by PW1, his permanent physical disability was assessed as 15.61%.
However, the Tribunal, has however, scaled down the percentage of disability of the petitioner to 10%, without assigning valid and cogent reasons.
The law is settled that, if the Tribunal is not satisfied with the disability certificate produced by the petitioner, the remedy is to refer him to a medical board or higher Authority.

(See Manikantan G. v. Janardhanan Nair and Others, 2021 (5) KHC 305). Having not done so, the Tribunal was not justified in scaling down the percentage of disability from what is shown in the disability 2025:KER:16357 certificate.

entities.text: Manikantan G. v. Janardhanan Nair and Others, 2021 (5) KHC 305
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. In Exhibit A5 disability certificate, PW1 specifically noted that because of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the percentage of disability suffered by him, he will not be able to perform the work of a driver and that he has got difficulty to drive four wheeler with pedals.

Since the petitioner was a driver of a goods carrier and because of the injuries sustained, he could not continue his profession as a driver of a goods carrier, though his permanent physical disability is noted as 15.61%
as assessed by PW1, his functional disability is much more.
Therefore, the functional disability is fixed as 25%.
15. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 58 years.

Therefore, 10% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Joseph vs Sivaraj on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8252865/

Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.2,97,000/-.

16. Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/- being the income for 5 months @
Rs.5000/-.
Since the notional income of the 2025:KER:16357 petitioner is re-fixed at Rs.10,000/-

,
towards loss of earning he is entitled to get a sum of Rs. 50,000/-(10,000x5months).
17.
Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.30,000/-
Towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.20,000/-. was awarded and towards 'extra nourishment' Rs.1,000/- was awarded.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
18. The petitioner sustained serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 12 days.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', 'loss of amenities of life' and 'extra nourishment' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.50,000/-, Rs.30,000/- and Rs.5,000/- respectively.
19.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
20. Therefore, the petitioner/appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.4,77,150/-, as modified and recalculated above and 2025
given in the table below, for easy reference:

Sl.
No. Head of Claim Amount awarded by Amount Awarded in Tribunal (in Rs.) Appeal (in Rs.) 1 Loss of earning 25,000/- 50,000/- (10000x5) 2

Transportation 2,000/-
2000/-
3 Extra nourishment 1,000/- 5,000/- 4 Damage to clothing and 500/- 500/- articles 5 Bystander expenses 1,500/- 1,500/- 6
Medical expenses 41,150/- 41,150/- 7 Pain and suffering 30,000/- 50,000/- 8 Loss due to disability 54,000/- 2,97,000/- 9 Loss of amenities 20,000/- 30,000/-

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and Respondent No.3 is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.4,77,150/- (Rupees four lakh seventy seven thousand one Joseph vs Sivaraj on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8252865/
4 hundred and fifty only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.

22. On Sd/-
C. PRATHEEP KUMAR, JUDGE sou.
